newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds were lower late on Friday after a very quiet session, with the long future trapped in a very tight range.
"Apart from a few buyers at the short end this morning we have not seen anything all day," a dealer said.
The long bond future moved in a 27 basis points range, as it lacked fuel to gain further when it hit a record high at 117.51.
The 10-year spread over Bunds was unmoved at 67 basis points
Dealers said that it was likely sideways trading would continue also on Monday given the lack of fresh domestic news.
The only focus next week will be June CPI's release.
"Next week, we'll look for any clues on the inflation trend," another dealer added.
The consumer price index, which rose 1.5 percent year-on- year in May, is generally seen likely to pick up a bit to around 1.6 percent, dealers said.
But recently Economy Secretary Cristobal Montoro said a refuelling of the inflation trend was not "necessary," in June.
